endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Establish a retention period for the data register after the AI solution itself is decommissioned.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: It is also important to have an EOL plan for patient data, data migration, archival, etc. and clarify whether end users will receive support in the AI solution’s absence (e.g., contact information, onboarding to a new solution, etc.).

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Use of open-source data or models;

endorsements.title: The Utility and Implications of Ambient Scribes in Primary Care
endorsements.quote: Lastly, procedures should be put in place that specify whether whole conversations should be saved, whether only utterances from one party are necessary, and for how long recordings are to be retained (eg, for auditing or retraining).

endorsements.title: Establishing responsible use of AI guidelines: a comprehensive case study for healthcare institutions
endorsements.quote: Crucially, we prohibited long-term storage and use of recordings because the recordings cannot be de-identified, thereby safeguarding the privacy and security of both patients and clinicians.

endorsements.title: Use of AI within COA linguistic validation and eCOA migration processes: analysis and good practice recommendations
endorsements.quote: Controlled storage or no storage of data If input data are either securely controlled in an effectively encrypted memory or purged from the system after the AI interaction has ended, the risk of data leakage is significantly reduced.

endorsements.title: Barriers and opportunities of scaling ambient AI scribes for clinical documentation across diverse healthcare settings
endorsements.quote: In the absence of explicit guidance, health systems need to define what to retain, the duration of retention, and access controls, with clear distinction between transient processing data and records incorporated into the medical records that are legally binding.

endorsements.title: Ethical Considerations in Personal Health Large Language Models
endorsements.quote: Tier 3 content would be temporarily retained only as needed for required safety audit, legally authorized safety review, or legal compliance and then deleted; and Tier 4 content would require explicit user authorization and periodic reconsent, with automatic deletion as the default absent active renewal.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence and Mental Health Services in Somalia: Opportunities and Health-System Considerations
endorsements.quote: Given the sensitivity and stigma often associated with mental health, Somalia should adopt a “minimum safe governance package” for any AI-enabled mental health tool: clear purpose limitation, data minimization, explicit consent where feasible, defined retention periods, and auditable access controls.

endorsements.title: Multimodal generative AI for pre-practicum mental health support competency development: a human-supervised framework for education-childcare partnerships
endorsements.quote: Real child- or family-related data require documented educational necessity, an appropriate lawful basis, institutional approval, restricted access, defined retention, secure storage, and verifiable deletion.

commentary.bottom_line: No study tests whether defining and executing retention, storage, and destruction plans for AI data reduces exposure risk, and no study documents the hazard itself. Support rests on ten endorsements from frameworks and commentaries, with one CHAI playbook rating it a must.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. All ten endorsements are frameworks or commentaries, which express expert agreement but cannot establish effect. Certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence, and the consistency of endorsements should not be read as a measure of benefit.

Several commentaries on ambient scribes describe the design choices a retention plan would need to settle. These include whether to save whole conversations or one party's speech, how long recordings are kept for auditing or retraining, and how transient processing data differs from records entered into the legal medical record. No study reports how such plans perform in practice.

The endorsements suggest that recordings which cannot be de-identified may carry privacy exposure, and one institution reports prohibiting their long-term storage. Because no study measures breaches, leakage, or misuse tied to retained AI data, the size of the risk and the degree to which deletion schedules lower it remain unknown.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare organizations with and without defined AI data retention and destruction plans, including at system decommissioning. Useful outcomes would be the volume of retained recordings and transcripts, adherence to deletion schedules, audit findings, and privacy incidents. Studies should also report the staff time and cost of carrying out these plans.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice in any population, so there is no evidence on Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy patients. One commentary raises data minimization and defined retention for mental health tools in a low-resource setting. Without studies, it is unknown whether retention practices protect these groups equally or whether their recorded conversations face different exposure.
